lemmas.statement: Within the declared list of 111 candidate sequences, no response of cost below 2 separates the collapsed pair. This is a finite statement over the declared list only. It does not assert that no constructor exists.

near_misses.claim: The Genesis finite statement is a constructor-theoretic impossibility of a task.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The statement quantifies only over the declared candidate list with a cost bound. It has no constructor, no accuracy limit, and does not range over all constructors.

near_misses.claim: Regime augmentation is a physical transformation of a system.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Regime augmentation changes the description regime, not the physical state of a system. This is the difference stated in the target.

open_obligations: No cited source maps cost-bounded response search to constructor existence, so no generator or relation could be grounded.

The cited Rust checkers are tests of the collapse barrier and the refinement separation. None is an operation, and I did not confirm that any covers the 111-candidate cost-below-2 claim, so none is cited.
A formal definition of task, constructor and accuracy for the finite Genesis setting is needed before any composition can be licensed.
Only an analogy is established. Whether the Genesis statement is a finite instance of a constructor-theoretic impossibility remains open.
